title: SDK resilience guardrails: pragmatic retry defaults, id-key semantics, and streaming resume playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: SDK users get confused about which errors to retry, how to choose backoff defaults, and when/how to provide idempotency keys across Python/TypeScript/Go. We also lack a consistent streaming resume contract and examples that demonstrate service-model-safe retries with minimal duplication. This ticket produces a single pragmatic playbook and default config that SDKs can adopt with small language-specific ergonomics, plus example snippets and a migration guide.
background: Over the last year we observed a pattern of client-side retries that either cause duplicated side effects for non-idempotent operations or are too conservative and surface transient failures to customers. Support and Red Team incidents show three recurring failure modes: transient infra errors (gateway timeouts, transient 5xx), throttling vs quota (429-like), and client-connection anomalies during streaming. There are also mismatched expectations across language SDKs about whether idempotency keys are required, optional, or auto-generated.
acceptance_criteria: Documented cross-sdk retry policy defaults (short, medium, long profiles) with numeric parameters and rationale
Idempotency key contract: scope, TTL, recommended key formats and examples for Python/TS/Go
Streaming resume contract defined: resume token shape, server compatibility notes, and client behavior for partial retry vs full restart
Error taxonomy mapping HTTP/gRPC errors + common infra signals to retryable/non-retryable buckets
SDK patches (Python/TS/Go) that add the default profiles as opt-out configuration and include examples in the repo
Migration guide for customers to opt into stricter deduplication semantics when enabling auto-retries
technical_notes: We prefer conservative defaults that favor availability for read/analysis calls and conservatism for mutating calls. Backoff profiles: short (3 retries, base=150ms, max=1s, jitter=full), medium (5 retries, base=300ms, max=5s, jitter=decorrelated), long (8 retries, base=500ms, max=20s). Idempotency key TTL: server retention 24 hours, recommended client TTL 48 hours to account for propagation delays. Streaming resume must include a monotonic frame index or byte-offset; clients MUST not automatically deduplicate content across resumed sessions unless the server explicitly marks frames as replay-safe.
implementation_plan: Draft RFC in repo/docs/sdks/retries-idkey-playbook.md and circulate to SDK leads
Approximate API surface: add RetryProfile enum and IdempotencyHint header; implement cross-language opt-out flag (enable_resilience_defaults = true)
Implement Python and TypeScript changes in side branches with unit + integration tests against local chaos harness
Add streaming resume tests with sequence numbers and server-side 'replay_safe' flag for edge case validation
Ship docs and code examples, coordinate blog/upgrade notes for next release
examples: Python example: client = RedwoodClient(retry_profile='medium', idempotency_generator=lambda req: req.user_id + ':' + req.timestamp)
TypeScript example: const client = new Client({ retryProfile: 'short', idempotencyStrategy: 'userTrace' }); // id-key added as X-Req-Id header
Go example: client.SetRetryPolicy(EnableResilienceDefaults(true)); client.WithIdempotencyKey(func(req) string { return fmt.Sprintf("%s:%d", req.User, time.Now().UnixNano()) })
error_taxonomy: Retryable - safe: 502, 503, 504, gRPC UNAVAILABLE, network timeouts; client may retry immediately using profile
Retryable - rate-limited: 429, 503 with rate headers; client should honor Retry-After when present and use medium/long profiles
Non-retryable - client: 400, 401, 403, 404 (unless specific operation marked idempotent)
Non-retryable - server-side permanent: 422 (invalid request body), 409 (conflict) unless operation documented as idempotent
Streaming transient: io.ErrUnexpectedEOF, connection reset -> attempt resume if resume token available, otherwise surface error
Ambiguous: 500 without idempotency marker -> default to no automatic retry for mutating endpoints; allow developer override
migration_notes: Default setting: enable_resilience_defaults=true for new SDK installs; existing customers get opt-in change with clear release note
Provide server-side log for id-key collisions and a dashboard metric to surface application-level duplicates post-rollout
Recommend customers with non-idempotent side-effects to either pass explicit idempotency keys scoped to the user/action or disable auto-retries on mutating routes
